title: How Leases Are Made — Section 107 TPA

content.overview: Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 prescribes how leases of immovable property are made. A lease of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, or reserving a yearly rent, can be made only by a registered instrument. All other leases of immovable property may be made either by a registered instrument or by oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession. Where a lease is made by a registered instrument, such instrument or instruments must be executed by both the lessor and the lessee.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Year to year / term > 1 year / yearly rent — registered instrument only? (2) Other leases — registered instrument or oral + delivery of possession? (3) Both parties execute registered instrument?
content.study:
s. 107 is the formality provision for leases defined in s. 105. The strict registration path applies to year-to-year leases, terms exceeding one year, and leases reserving yearly rent. Shorter or other leases may use oral agreement with delivery of possession.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Mandatory registration class
sections.body: Year to year; term exceeding one year; or reserving yearly rent — only by registered instrument.

sections.heading: Other leases
sections.body: May be made by registered instrument or by oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.body: Where made by registered instrument, both lessor and lessee must execute.

sections.heading: Link to s. 105
sections.body: s. 105 defines lease; s. 107 prescribes how it is made.

sections.heading: Exam method
sections.body: Classify the lease term/rent reservation first, then apply the matching formality rule.

examples.title: Three-year lease
examples.body: Lease for three years — term exceeds one year — must be by registered instrument under s. 107.

hypotheticals.question: Can a two-year lease of a shop be made by oral agreement and delivery of possession alone?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. A term exceeding one year falls in the mandatory registration class under s. 107.

misconceptions.trap: Every lease can be oral if possession is delivered.
misconceptions.correction: Year-to-year, term > 1 year, or yearly rent leases require a registered instrument.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain how leases are made under TPA s. 107.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Mandatory registration class; other leases oral + possession or registered; both parties execute registered instrument.
